memo.verdict: PARK. High conviction. Direction neutral. Overall grade [D]. The memo parks SNR-GB (Senior plc) on investability, not on business quality: Senior is under a recommended cash acquisition by Zeus UK Bidco (Blackstone and Tinicum) at 297.85p per share, announced 7 April 2026, approved by 99.7% of votes cast on 26 May 2026, with 10 of 12 required regulatory and antitrust approvals secured by August 2026 and completion expected by year-end 2026. At a live price of 293.0p (14 August 2026) the gross spread to the offer is 4.85p, or 1.66%, over roughly four months. The memo's position is that this is a merger-arbitrage spread, not an investment case, and that a 12 to 20 name concentrated long-only book cannot express a fundamental view in an instrument whose price is pinned to a fixed cash consideration. Three named re-open triggers, and nothing else re-opens the file. Trigger 1: the scheme lapses, is withdrawn, or is blocked in either outstanding jurisdiction, at which point the file re-opens within five working days. Trigger 2: a competing bidder emerges and the shares trade materially through 297.85p on a live contest. Trigger 3: completion slips beyond Q1 2027, which the earnings-review family names as the point at which Senior would operate standalone with suspended capital returns and elevated advisory costs. Monitoring cadence is a weekly check of the two outstanding antitrust jurisdictions until completion or lapse. Two downstream actions. (1) Investment Analyst monitors the two outstanding antitrust jurisdictions weekly and re-opens the file within five working days of any lapse. (2) Assistant Portfolio Manager moves SNR-GB to the delisting watch list and removes it from the active triage queue by 24 August 2026.
case: The memo's argument runs in five steps.

Step one, the decisive fact is not in the accounts. Senior's board unanimously recommended a cash acquisition at 297.85p on 7 April 2026. Shareholders approved the scheme with 99.7% of votes cast on 26 May 2026, which removes the shareholder-approval risk that normally keeps an arbitrage spread open. Ten of twelve regulatory and antitrust approvals were secured by August 2026, with completion expected by year-end. The earnings-review family's own conclusion states that the buyout renders traditional fundamental analysis moot and terminated the independent public company investment case.

Step two, the arithmetic. At 293.0p against 297.85p the residual return is 4.85p, or 1.66%, over roughly four months. That is the entire remaining change-from-current. The memo cross-checks the offer price: 297.85p across 419,418,082 ordinary shares implies about £1.25bn, consistent with the £1.2bn headline. The consensus target of 287.5p sits below both the live price and the offer, so the sell-side sees no standalone upside either. Element E1 Required Attribute 2 Core Question 4 grades F on this alone.
counter_case: Three counters are carried at full strength.

The merger-arbitrage counter, which the memo names as the strongest. A 1.66% gross spread over four months annualises to roughly 5%, which beats cash, and it sits behind a court-sanctioned scheme with 99.7% shareholder approval and ten of twelve approvals already granted. Short interest is below the UK 0.5% reporting threshold, there is no published short-seller campaign, and institutional and event-driven capital has been accumulating. On probability-weighted terms this is a high-confidence, short-duration return. What would have to be true for it to win: the reader would need a merger-arbitrage mandate with position-level hedging and a tolerance for binary break risk. The memo rejects it on mandate rather than on merit, holding that a capped 1.66% upside cannot justify a position slot in a 12 to 20 name concentrated book whatever the completion probability.
triggers: Re-open triggers. A scheme lapse, withdrawal or block in either of the two outstanding jurisdictions, re-opening the file within five working days. A competing bidder trading the shares materially through 297.85p on a live contest. Completion slipping beyond Q1 2027, at which point Senior operates standalone with suspended capital returns and elevated advisory costs.

What would make it a buy after a lapse. Not 293.0p. The memo's position is that a lapse removes the offer floor and reprices the equity toward standalone value, with the risks family modelling a stressed 12.0x EV/EBITA against an 18.0x recovery multiple. A lapse followed by a de-rating toward the Deutsche Bank bear case of 215p would restore genuine change-from-current.

Operating monitorables carried forward. Aerospace margin progression from 13.1% in H1 2026 toward the mid-teens medium-term target. The Aerostructures earnout, up to £50m of the £200m enterprise value, contingent on the divested unit's performance. The 2027 Class 8 cliff-edge risk after the EPA-2027 regulatory pre-buy pulls demand forward. Full-year cash conversion recovering from 63% in H1 2026 toward the above-85% target.

Data gaps declared. The factset-valuation file is flagged stale in the assembled context, so the 22.3x forward price-to-earnings and 90th valuation percentile carry a currency caveat; no external source was substituted. The 52-week high of 318.2p sits above the 297.85p offer price and the dashboard feed does not explain it; it is reported as given and not reconciled. No web source, estimate or peer figure was used for any price, valuation or sell-side datapoint.

Source conflicts reconciled. The earnings-review family states 297.85p in its executive summary and conclusion and 225p in its section 5; 297.85p is preferred because 297.85p across 419,418,082 shares gives about £1.25bn, consistent with the stated £1.2bn headline, while 225p would imply about £944m, close to the pre-offer market capitalisation. The risks family states North American revenue at 62% in section 15 and 58% in its executive summary; 62% is preferred, consistent with the section 15 currency table, the change-forces family and the master digest.

Flags raised for corpus repair. The 44-risks family for SNR-GB should be re-run and quarantined: it was produced on 8 August 2026 with completeness WARN and no quality flag set, so the identity defect passed the mechanical check. IPN-FR resolves to Ipsen, a pharmaceutical company, inside the Aerostructures and Tier-2 Aerospace Suppliers cohort; it is excluded from every comparison and flagged for taxonomy repair. The assembled coverage note records "Above-floor reports present: none", which is wrong: four above-floor families are on disk and all four were read.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
